title: First pay sent home and first return to Memphis with the USO
summary: Her first $6 week sent $2 to her mother; she returned to Memphis only with the USO show and was praised in the paper; she praises Southerners and says she kept sending money.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: And in the meantime, I forgot to tell you, now when I got that job in Chicago, there when I went there looking for Ellen Winston, you know, and the lady gave me the job peeling potatoes, she gave me $6.00 a week, and I sent $2.00 home to my mother. That first payday, I sent my mother $2.00.
I was going to ask you, when did you -- at some point, I gather, you must have gone back to visit -- back to Memphis.
Back to Memphis? You know the first time I've ever been back to Memphis was with the USO show.

That's right. I went back to Memphis, and let me tell you something, I went back to Memphis with the show, and the commercial appeal -- the Sunday paper, big white paper, had a big headline, "Memphian makes good," and wrote me up. The nicest thing you ever saw in your life. They were so proud of me.

You can say what you want to say about the Southerner, but the Southerner, if he's your friend, he's your friend. He's all right. You know how you stand with a Southerner. I'm telling you, I'm telling you what God loves. A Southerner, if he doesn't like you, he's not two-faced. He lets you know he
doesn't like you, so you stay out of his way. But if he does like you, don't let anybody bother you. They're fine people. Fine people.
How come you never went home, when you were making all that money?

I was making all that money, but I tell you what, I was -- everytime I'd get ready to do something, like if I'm working in Dreamland, if I'd want to go home, I'd get an offer to go overseas, or I'd get an offer to go some place else. I really didn't have any time to go home. Although my mother heard from me every week of my life. She got money. Oh, sure, I sent my mother money every -- I sent my mother so much money I hope I saved that letter she told me, for God's sake, stop sending me -- I almost want to cry sometime. Told me to stop sending her money. She started going to the bank. Now, can you beat that? That's what she told me.
